title: Categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone: ECoG auditory oddball in 6 epilepsy patients (Si, Zhou & Hong 2017)
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six patients with medically intractable epilepsy who passively listened to a two-deviant auditory oddball sequence of synthesized Mandarin /i/ syllables. The standard was a level tone (T1), and the two deviants were a cross-category rising tone (T2) and a within-category level tone, each equidistant from the standard. The dataset supports investigation of the cortical network underlying categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone. It is organized in iEEG-BIDS without signal processing.
methods_description: ECoG was recorded with subdural surface grids, placed by clinical need only, using a g.USBamp amplifier at 1200 Hz with a 0.1 Hz high-pass filter and a 50 Hz notch. Stimuli were presented in an oddball paradigm of 500 trials (250 for S6) with an onset-to-onset interval of 1100 ms and 5% jitter, while patients watched a silent movie. Triggers were recorded on a dedicated channel and decoded into events.
